lead.headline: Jury convicts Duane Davis of first-degree murder in Tupac Shakur's killing
lead.dek: Deliberations took less than three hours; Davis, 63, is the only person ever charged in the 30-year-old case.
body: A Clark County jury on Monday found Duane "Keffe D" Davis, 63, guilty of first-degree murder with a deadly weapon in the 1996 drive-by killing of Tupac Shakur, deliberating less than three hours after a nine-day Las Vegas trial. Davis is the only person ever charged in a shooting that went unresolved for nearly 30 years.

Shakur, 25, was stopped at a red light near the Strip on Sept. 7, 1996, when a white Cadillac pulled alongside and shots were fired; he died six days later. Prosecutors built the case on Davis's own repeated public accounts that he rode in the Cadillac and handed a gun into the back seat, calling the shooting retaliation for a beating of his nephew by Shakur's entourage earlier that evening.

The jury heard 24 prosecution witnesses against three for the defense, which argued no footage or records placed Davis in Las Vegas that night. Sentencing is set for October, NPR reported, and Davis faces up to life in prison; CBS reported Shakur's sister wept in the courtroom as the verdict was read.

briefs.headline: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll steps down after 18 months
briefs.summary: The White House confirmed the departure Monday night without giving a reason and named no successor; NPR reported tensions with the defense secretary's office.

briefs.headline: Flash flooding kills 2 at the Grand Canyon; Phantom Ranch closes
briefs.summary: Weekend floods on Bright Angel Creek destroyed most of its footbridges and about 40% of the canyon's waterline; 82 people were flown out and one is still missing.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court lets White House ballroom construction continue
briefs.summary: The order keeps the $400M, 90,000-square-foot project moving while the challenge proceeds, after lower courts found it lacked congressional approval.

briefs.headline: Trump posts AI videos of a Kharg Island strike that did not happen
briefs.summary: No attack on Iran's main oil terminal, which ships about 90% of its crude, was reported; the weekend's real strikes hit minelaying forces near Larak Island.

briefs.headline: Flood toll in Nepal and Tibet passes 1,000 as counts settle
briefs.summary: Nepal reports 987 dead and 3,916 missing, down from 4,247 after reconciliation; about 500 hydropower workers are still believed trapped in tunnels.

briefs.headline: Russia hits Kyiv a sixth straight night, killing 12
briefs.summary: Six rail workers died when ballistic missiles struck rail facilities; Ukraine says it downed 199 of the 218 drones and most missiles in the barrage.

briefs.headline: Hundreds bury 4 victims of the Kenscoff attack that killed 47
briefs.summary: Sunday funerals followed the release of six children and seven women taken Aug. 23; dozens remain held and police are probing complicity or negligence.

briefs.headline: MARL developers ask the PSC to push its ruling to May 2027
briefs.summary: NextEra sought a 77-day delay from March 6 after commission staff flagged five route changes proposed weeks before the evidentiary hearing.

briefs.headline: Kirkpatrick joins the state Supreme Court, hears cases Wednesday
briefs.summary: The longtime Raleigh County circuit judge was sworn in Monday to the seat of the late Justice Tim Armstead, with eight cases on his first docket.

briefs.headline: America 250 invoices near $2.2M, past the fund's $2M budget
briefs.summary: Reporting published Saturday itemized $737,065 for a Capitol light show, $350,000 for a Ferris wheel and $300,000 for the band Alabama over four July days.

regional.item: A 63-year-old man was arrested on assault charges after confronting Mason County deputies with a handgun Sunday; a deputy fired four shots.
Nitro police identified a suspect in the elementary school playground vandalism, with middle and high school students under investigation.
Wood County has all 275 poll workers lined up for the Nov. 3 general election after consolidating nine precincts.

away.item: Damaged electrical equipment cut power to about 200 downtown Bennington addresses Friday; restoration was expected by mid-afternoon.

hotspots.item: The Webster Springs fire department's Bergoo Bash, an ATV poker run with food trucks and live music, runs Saturday on Bergoo Road.
Three Pender subdivisions totaling 1,354 homes, 90 of them in Topsail Township, go before county boards this week alongside a sand-mine expansion.

briefs.headline: Croft Road permit dispute heads back to council Sept. 9
briefs.summary: The city issued a building permit in error for a Hart-area home whose deck violates setbacks; council deadlocked 4-4 on the variance that would legalize it.

briefs.headline: Seventh MLA leaves the B.C. Conservative caucus in two weeks
briefs.summary: Chilliwack-Cultus Lake's A'a:liya Warbus will sit as an independent, citing poor communication and decisions members learned of on social media.

briefs.headline: Liberals sweep three by-elections and reclaim a majority at 173
briefs.summary: Dairy farmer Daniel Gobeil took Chicoutimi-Le Fjord from the Conservatives with 51.3%; wins in Beaches-East York and North Vancouver-Capilano followed.

briefs.headline: Roman telescope completes its first course-correction burn
briefs.summary: The three-minute burn at midday Monday adjusted the observatory's path toward its L2 orbit point; a second adjustment may follow this week, NASA said.

briefs.headline: Thylacine skull points to a hunting style with no modern match
briefs.summary: A Nature Communications analysis finds the Tasmanian tiger paired a fox-like snout with a snapping bite built for small prey, not sheep, researchers said.

briefs.headline: Trial ties freshwater swimming to rashes and stomach illness
briefs.summary: In a 2,368-person randomized study at four Hungarian sites meeting EU standards, swimmers reported skin complaints at twice the rate of those ashore.

briefs.headline: EU designates ChatGPT a very large search engine under the DSA
briefs.summary: OpenAI declared over 45 million monthly EU users, triggering four months to meet systemic-risk rules covering minors, elections and illegal content.

briefs.headline: Sony and Warner music publishers sue Anthropic over training
briefs.summary: Thirty-five publishers alleged Thursday that Claude trained on pirated compositions, seeking up to $150,000 per work; Anthropic said it will defend itself.

briefs.headline: Apple files new evidence in its trade-secrets case against OpenAI
briefs.summary: A Monday filing alleges a former engineer took a confidential circuit schematic to OpenAI to train an engineering agent, then destroyed evidence.
